In algebraic geometry, a '''Coble surface''' was defined by {{harvtxt|Dolgachev|Zhang|2001}} to be a  smooth rational projective surface with empty [[anti-canonical linear system]] |&minus;K| and non-empty anti-bicanonical linear system |&minus;2K|. An example of a Coble surface is the [[blowing up]] of the projective plane at the 10 nodes of a [[Coble curve]].<ref>{{Citation | doi=10.1353/ajm.2001.0002 | last1=Dolgachev | first1=Igor V. | last2=Zhang | first2=De-Qi | title=Coble Rational Surfaces | jstor=25099046 | publisher=The Johns Hopkins University Press | year=2001 | journal=[[American Journal of Mathematics]] | issn=0002-9327 | volume=123 | issue=1 | pages=79–114|mr=1827278| arxiv=math/9909135 }}</ref>
